notes: MMR-32 heroes and rosters (docs/heroes.md). Owners: HeroFactory and CharacterTemplateResolver (src/MNBL.ProceduralWorld/Campaign/). Lords (the planned members of campaign.json v2 houses, mercenary companies and outlaw clans, their minors and dead parents, MMR-279/280) are XML heroes (NPCCharacters + Heroes) for the MMR-30 registry; notables and companions are runtime creation intents, because the installed engine creates them through HeroCreator at new game (MMR-34 replaces the vanilla spawns and instantiates these with HeroCreator.CreateSpecialHero(template, settlement, null, null, age) and SetName, keeping the intent id in its own map: the engine mints the StringId). Body ranges, equipment, skills and troops are installed templates; identities and names come from the world.

streams.rule:
value(stream, version, world prefix, entity, draw) = first 8 bytes of sha256("mnbl.hero-stream/1
" + stream + "
" + version + "
" + prefix + "
" + entity + "
" + draw), big-endian. Each purpose has its own stream; re-versioning one changes what it draws and what is derived from that: a notable's sex follows its template and a synthesized name follows the sex. Ownership, occupations, clans, kin, lord ages and sexes (campaign.json v2) use no stream; lord personalities use population.json's traits stream.

lords.templates: the presentation culture's lord_templates (installed is_template Lord NPCCharacters), one drawn from the templates stream; the hero keeps the template's body range (face key template), skill set and its traits other than the personality ones, and takes the world's id, name, culture, age and sex (campaign.json v2 age and female, FWGC++ sex and mapped age). Its personality traits (Mercy, Valor, Honor, Generosity, Calculating) are never copied from the template: each XML hero draws one vector of population.json lordTraits.joint, weighted by count, from the population traits stream seeded by its hero id (RT-05)
lords.equipment: no installed lord template is female and their rosters carry men's gear, so a man wears the template's equipment sets and a woman one battle and one civilian roster of her culture flagged IsLordTemplate and IsFemaleTemplate (never child or teenager), from the templates stream. Every worn item must exist, fit its slot and be usable by the wearer's sex
lords.bodies: an XML hero gets an explicit body: HeroBodies (in game) draws it with BodyProperties.GetRandomBodyProperties(race 0, sex, the template's body range, the range's hair/beard/tattoo tags, seed from the bodies stream). Hero.Deserialize otherwise gives every hero of a template the range minimum
lords.bound: the XML lords are exactly the Lords campaign.json v2 plans (its census counts them): no lord, spouse or heir is synthesized here
lords.race: every hero uses the installed human body; the source raceId is kept as metadata (custom skeletons are out of scope)

kin.rule: campaign.json v2 plans every family link (MMR-279): spouse on both heroes, father and mother. A dead parent (alive false) is an XML hero of its house with alive="false", outside the census and every party and lord rule. A planned minor is accepted only with both parents set
kin.minors: a minor keeps its template's body range (HeroBodies ages it) and wears a battle roster of its culture's lord rosters for its sex and, as civilian equipment, the culture's noble child roster below teenagerAge or teenager roster from it (IsLordTemplate with IsChildEquipmentTemplate or IsTeenagerEquipmentTemplate), as the engine's child generator dresses its children
kin.census: the instantiated houses, adult lords, minors, dead parents, company and outlaw members and wanderers equal the campaign.json v2 census; a mismatch refuses the build

notables.targetsSource: DefaultNotableSpawnModel.GetTargetNotableCountForSettlement (installed IL); NotablesCampaignBehavior.SpawnNotablesAtGameStart creates exactly these at new game, so recruitment, workshops and issues expect them
notables.rule: source notables fill their settlement first, in uid order, up to the cap of their occupation; a source notable beyond the cap is not instantiated (disposition bounded). Every target not met by source notables is filled with synthesized notables. Castles have none
notables.templates: the settlement culture's notable_templates of that occupation; the template decides the sex

companions.rule: the companions are campaign.json v2 wanderers[] (MMR-279), exactly W = census.wanderers of them, the smallest integer not below the float32 product 0.6f x towns (CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnNewGameCreated, installed IL; RT-04). Each keeps its FWGC++ sex and planned age and an epithet in its name; none is synthesized here
companions.home: a town of the companion's presentation culture (templates stream), else any town
companions.templates: MMR-287's backstory-safe pool (population.json wanderers, WandererPool): the culture's safe is_template Wanderer NPCCharacters of the wanderer's sex, least used first, else its fallback culture's (recorded)

roles.recruitment: basic_troop and elite_basic_troop trees: notables offer volunteers of the settlement culture
roles.garrison: default_party_template: GarrisonTroopsCampaignBehavior.FillGarrisonPartyOnNewGame fills garrisons from Town.Culture.DefaultPartyTemplate (installed IL)
roles.bandits: every installed bandit culture (is_bandit): bandit_* troops and bandit_boss_party_template
roles.naval: settlement_patrol_template_coastal, fishing_party_template, shipwright, shipyard_worker and available_ship_hulls (NavalDLC)

troops.banditClans: the default_party_template of every installed bandit clan (Factions.xml is_bandit), from which BanditSpawnCampaignBehavior spawns
troops.rule: for every presentation culture and every installed bandit culture, each root and every troop reachable through upgrade targets and party template stacks (and the ship hulls under ship_hulls) must resolve, with its equipment, items (existing, fitting their slot, usable by the troop's sex), face key template and skill set; an upgrade cycle, a missing target or a broken required root refuses the build. A broken optional hero template or lord roster is excluded from its pool and reported; only an empty pool refuses

characterCreation.cultures: CharacterCreationCampaignBehavior.InitializeCharacterCreationCultures adds aserai, battania, empire, khuzait, sturgia and vlandia, and NavalCharacterCreationCampaignBehavior adds nord (installed IL). GeneratedCharacterCreation registers a content handler after both (priority 2000; theirs are 800 and 1000) that leaves only the cultures the generated world presents through. The installed culture screen (CharacterCreationCultureStageVM.SortCultureList) places the six vanilla cultures with Enumerable.Single and crashes when one is missing, so while a restricted list is active a Harmony prefix skips that sort
characterCreation.origins: parent options check the culture; later menus check the parent occupation (education: urban or rural) and the youth options set the title type that names the player's creation rosters (player_char_creation_<culture>_<title>_<m|f>). The in-game audit selects every parent origin, evaluates every later menu for it, selects every youth option for its title type and resolves every menu character's rosters and items. The start position (CultureObject.StartingPoint) belongs to MMR-34
